summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, type 1 diabetes with functioning pancreatic transplants, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted after two syncopal episodes associated with dizziness and a supratherapeutic INR of 15. She presented with severe anemia (hemoglobin 5.2) and hyperkalemia (potassium 7.1). She received vitamin K, multiple units of packed red blood cells, and hemodialysis to stabilize her condition. An elevated troponin and chest pressure three days before discharge raised concern for cardiac ischemia, but cardiology determined it was likely demand ischemia from anemia rather than an acute event. GI evaluation with endoscopy and colonoscopy showed no active bleeding source, and the anemia was attributed to diffuse loss from anticoagulation. Her INR was successfully normalized and bridged from heparin to warfarin, reaching 3.4 at discharge. She was evaluated for chronic hand pain, with imaging and rheumatology consultation suggesting vascular etiology rather than autoimmune disease. She was discharged home with services, alert and ambulatory, on warfarin, aspirin, and home medications, with follow-up planned in cardiology, vascular surgery, and GI.
